A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-compression work, with matching authors, methods and many identical results. Their text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and compression results for 500 LoRAs, serving-throughput experiments, and appendix analyses of reconstruction, convergence and generalization.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds clustering experiments and revised serving-throughput measurements.

M1.justification: v2 adds explicit learned clustering with separate shared bases for each cluster. Section 3.2 and Appendix A.3 introduce initialization through joint diagonalization and k-means, followed by alternating per-cluster compression and reassignment. This substantially extends the procedure; individual SVD and the original JD methods remain.

E1.justification: v2 removes the fixed-basis evaluation of unseen/new LoRAs on ten additional task IDs from v1 Appendix F.11 and Table 13. The principal Natural Instructions tasks, LoRA-Hub evaluation and Shakespeare serving workload remain. Newly discussed edge-device applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The task-performance comparisons retain the base model, uncompressed LoRA, SVD and TIES-merging. However, SVD-4 and SVD-8 disappear from the throughput comparison shown in v1 Figure 4. v2 retains the uncompressed vLLM comparator and focuses that comparison on JD configurations.

E3.justification: Serving experiments change from an A100 80GB with a 30% memory cap to an H100 80GB with a 40% cap. v2 explicitly matches baseline GPU residency to compressed memory usage, extends the serving sweep from 64–1024 to 4–1024 LoRAs, and introduces clustering configurations and a 99% performance-preservation criterion. These materially revise the evaluation conditions.

E4.justification: Appendix F and Figure 5 add rank/cluster-count sensitivity analyses relating reconstruction error to compression for 100 and 500 LoRAs. Conversely, the unseen-adapter projection study is removed. This substantially changes the evidence about scalability and incremental deployment, while retaining convergence, trained-versus-random reconstruction and LoRA-Hub analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds throughput error bars in Figure 1 without specifying their statistical meaning. Both versions retain the three-seed mean-and-standard-deviation statement for task experiments, but the new clustering rows omit uncertainty values. There is no documented increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds clustering results across Tables 3–10, replaces throughput results under changed conditions, and removes unseen-adapter outcomes. Matched older table values remain unchanged. Some new relative and absolute scores do not reconcile: for 500 LoRAs, rank 64 and seven clusters, task039 has relative score 1.12 in Table 3, whereas Table 4 gives 98.00 against a 95.00 LoRA baseline.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a formal clustered reconstruction objective and parameter-complexity comparison between multiple rank-r clusters and one higher-rank basis. The existing proposition, theorem, corollary, proofs and JD derivations remain substantively unchanged after relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions shift from individual SVD plus joint compression to joint compression extended by clustering as a central scalability contribution. The headline serving claim changes from over 2× throughput and 75% of single-LoRA throughput to 1.6× and 80%, respectively, under the revised evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 explains clustering as a remedy for growing shared-basis reconstruction error and adds configuration guidance and limitations at much larger collection sizes. It removes v1's explicit limitations appendix and discussion of degraded performance when inserting new LoRAs into an existing basis, including the practical recommendations arising from that finding.

D1.justification: New appendices document GPU parameter accounting, baseline residency limits for each serving configuration, and reconstruction-based selection of cluster counts and ranks. Appendix A.3 supplies clustering initialization and stopping details. Existing training splits, quantization configuration, LoRA hyperparameters and promised code/adapter release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Apple foundation models, fine-tuning services from OpenAI, TogetherAI and Predibase, and Yadav et al.'s 2024 survey. These broaden deployment motivation and related-work context; the established PEFT, compression and model-merging positioning largely remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and serving analysis are substantially rewritten, SVD is repositioned as a baseline and limiting case of clustering, and the method narrative and appendices are reorganized. The standalone limitations and acknowledgements sections disappear. These changes extend beyond renumbering or added scientific content alone.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 2 and 4 are redesigned, including new axes, error bars and highlighted performance-preserving regions; Figure 5 adds a two-panel clustering analysis. Tables gain clustering blocks, the unseen-adapter table is removed, and the duplicated exact-match table is deleted. Typography, headings and table placement also change throughout.

improvement.justification: Clustering and the explicit memory-matched serving protocol strengthen the paper's scalability analysis. However, unexplained discrepancies between new relative and absolute scores in Tables 3–4, together with missing clustering uncertainty, limit confidence in the performance-preservation criterion. Removing the unseen-adapter failure study and its limitations also reduces practical completeness. These benefits and unresolved weaknesses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
